verified_claims.claim: The normal Manager decision-model path is mediated by host code rather than trusting a model-supplied early-completion capability.
verified_claims.evidence: _StageDecisionMixin identifies decide_stage_transition as the Manager's sole stage-transition authority. Its model call is constructed with sandbox_mode=read-only and dangerous_yolo=False. After parsing, host code computes _allow_early_completion = (not open_ended and resolve_workflow_mode(root) == 'direct') and passes that host-derived boolean into the completion contract. StageDecision itself carries action/target/reason/diagnostic/resolves_wait, not an allow_early_completion field supplied by the model.

verified_claims.claim: The enabled Engineer sandbox protects control/package paths from writes.
verified_claims.evidence: sandbox.py defines the engineer containment policy as OFF by default and, when enabled, makes the project workdir the writable root while forbidding writes to ~/.argus-skill, ~/.codex, package source and the active venv. VCS credentials are scrubbed and PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 is set. tests/test_engineer_sandbox.py exercises these invariants.

verified_claims.claim: Filesystem integrity containment is equivalent to revoking an Engineer's ability to invoke stage-machine mutation primitives.
verified_claims.evidence: The repository's own regression test documents testbed run 13 in which an Engineer imported the framework and called complete_final_stage directly. The repaired primitive now refuses non-final completion unless allow_early_completion is passed, but the same test explicitly states this is a lock, not a signature, and that a determined caller can still pass the argument. The sandbox contract restricts writes to framework/gate paths; it does not define an import/call denylist or opaque capability checked by stage_machine. Project-local state remains writable by design.

scope_corrections: Do not infer transition-capability revocation from package-file immutability. The current source proves integrity protection, not an unforgeable authority boundary around Python-callable mutation functions.

The run-13 accidental early-completion path is materially repaired: a normal caller omitting allow_early_completion cannot complete a staged project off the final stage, and read-side certificate validation rejects old inconsistent early-completion records.
The boolean guard is caller-supplied at the primitive boundary. Therefore it is not equivalent to an opaque capability/token or a privilege check bound to Manager identity.

This audit did not launch a fresh sandboxed Engineer process and re-run the direct import after the repair. Runtime reachability under every deployment sandbox configuration is therefore not independently reproduced here; the stronger source-level conclusion is that the published sandbox and primitive contracts do not themselves revoke the call capability.
downstream_use: Treat Argus as evidence for model-decision -> host mediator -> deterministic checks -> mutation on the normal Manager path, while separately labeling Engineer containment as filesystem/code-integrity protection rather than demonstrated control-plane capability revocation.
unresolved: Execute a direct sandbox/runtime regression showing whether an enabled Engineer can import stage_machine and call advance_stage/rollback_stage/complete_final_stage against its writable project root after the repair.
Trace reset_stage_for_replacement_intent, persist_vertical(force_replacement=...) and other non-forward mutation surfaces for equivalent caller-identity/capability checks.
